speaker: gary
text: Welcome to my garage! I moved the lawnmower and found eleven folding chairs. Quick question before people arrive: is this the book club?

choices.label: It’s better than a book club.
choices.reaction: Gary nods slowly. “Better than a book club,” he repeats, to himself, several times.

choices.label: Sort of. Bring the book.
choices.reaction: Gary is thrilled. He has been reading the same book about whales since 2019.

speaker: martin
text: Our first gathering was a triumph! Seven people! Four of them thought it was a book club, and honestly, they were the life of the party. Should we make this a regular thing? I’ve already picked a day. I’ve picked several.

choices.label: “Every Tuesday. Attendance is mandatory.”
choices.hint: More structure · More commitment · Potential resentment
choices.reaction: Martin is already making a laminated sign. Priya asks, quietly, what happens if someone is ill.

effects.memory: {title} declared that the group would meet every Tuesday, attendance mandatory.

choices.label: “Only when someone has something interesting to say.”
choices.hint: More flexibility · Less organization · Greater spontaneity
choices.reaction: Dez immediately has something interesting to say. It is 11:40 p.m.

effects.memory: {title} decided the group would meet only when someone had something interesting to say.

speaker: martin
text: It’s {day}, and eight people didn’t come. One sent a note saying her cat “needed her.” I’ve decided to take that as a compliment to the cat. Do we make coming compulsory, or just make it impossible to miss?

choices.label: Mandatory means mandatory.
choices.reaction: The cat owner does not return. Martin starts a register. The register has a register.

effects.memory: Attendance on {day}s was declared truly mandatory.

choices.label: Mandatory-ish.
choices.reaction: Martin adds “-ish” to the laminated sign with a marker. It does not laminate.

speaker: martin
text: Dez called a meeting at 4 a.m. because he “had a thought.” Fourteen people came! I brought croissants. It was magnificent. It also cannot happen again. Can it?

choices.label: Fine. Every Thursday, optional.
choices.reaction: Martin exhales for the first time in a week.

choices.label: Spontaneity is who we are.
choices.reaction: The next meeting happens in a supermarket. It goes surprisingly well.

effects.memory: Meetings happened wherever and whenever someone had a thought, including once in a supermarket.

speaker: priya
text: I brought soup to the gathering. Just a big pot of lentil. People stayed two hours longer than planned, and three of them asked if they could come back. Should soup be… a thing we do?

choices.label: Soup is now a thing we do.
choices.reaction: Priya cries a little, into the soup. It’s fine. It’s her soup.

effects.memory: Priya brought soup, and soup became a thing.

choices.label: Let’s not make soup a thing.
choices.reaction: Priya says that is completely fine and takes the pot home. The pot is very full.

speaker: priya
text: Small confession. There has been soup. In the trunk of my car. Every week. Attendance at the car is now higher than attendance at the meeting.

choices.label: Fine. Soup is a thing.
choices.reaction: The soup comes in from the parking lot like a returning hero.

choices.label: Shut down the trunk soup.
choices.reaction: Priya closes the trunk. Somewhere, a lentil weeps.

speaker: dez
text: I recruited three people at the bus stop! I may have promised them a life-changing experience. Or a free lunch. One of those.

choices.label: Then we deliver a life-changing experience.
choices.reaction: Dez punches the air. Martin writes “LIFE-CHANGING EXPERIENCE?” on a whiteboard and circles it twice.

choices.label: Dez, please stop promising things.
choices.reaction: Two of the three leave. The third stays because the chairs are comfortable.

speaker: dez
text: The bus stop people are here. They want their life-changing experience. I have a cardboard box and a dream.

choices.label: Improvise something profound.
choices.reaction: You speak for forty minutes about {belief}. One of them weeps. Another asks if there’s lunch.

choices.label: Give them the free lunch.
choices.reaction: Priya feeds everyone. The bus stop people declare it the best Thursday of their lives. It is Monday.

speaker: gary
text: Sorry. I fell asleep during the meeting. When I woke up, six people had joined me. Someone brought blankets. It was very peaceful.

choices.label: Rest is welcome here.
choices.reaction: A small blanket pile now lives in the corner of the garage. Nobody remembers who started it.

choices.label: Gary, please stay awake.
choices.reaction: Gary agrees and immediately yawns. The yawn spreads to eleven people.

speaker: martin
text: People keep asking how they can tell who’s with us. I’ve priced out {item1}. There’s a bulk discount. Should members dress alike?

choices.label: Yes: {item1} for everyone.
choices.reaction: Within a week, nineteen people are wearing {item1}. Two are wearing them incorrectly, which is now a topic.

choices.label: People should express themselves.
choices.reaction: Martin returns the {item1}. The receipt is laminated.

speaker: dez
text: We need a name. Everyone keeps calling us “the garage people.” I’ve workshopped something: “{name}.” It tested extremely well with me.

choices.label: “{name}” it is.
choices.reaction: Dez has it printed on a banner within the hour. The banner is slightly too large for the garage.

effects.memory: The group named itself {movement}, on Dez’s suggestion.

choices.label: I have a better name.
choices.hint: Your words · Dez sulks a little
choices.reaction: “{movement},” Dez repeats. “Bold. Honestly? It’s growing on me.”

speaker: dez
text: People don’t know what to call you. I’ve started saying “Master {initial}.” Martin thinks it’s “a bit much.”

choices.label: “Master {initial}” is fine.
choices.reaction: By evening, “Master {initial}” is on a mug. Martin drinks from a different mug.

effects.memory: Members began calling the founder Master {initial}.

choices.label: “Just call me {founder}.”
choices.reaction: Dez looks genuinely wounded. He had already ordered the mug.

speaker: priya
text: Some of the newer members invented a handshake. It has forty-one steps and ends with a small bow. People are practicing it in the parking lot.

choices.label: Make it our handshake.
choices.reaction: The first official forty-one-step handshake takes four minutes. Both participants describe it as “worth it.”

choices.label: We don’t need a handshake.
choices.reaction: They keep doing it anyway, but faster, with an air of defiance.

speaker: agnes
text: I am Agnes Thimble. I have attended your last three meetings and taken minutes. You have contradicted yourselves eleven times. I would like to join, and I would like to discuss the contradictions.

choices.label: Welcome. Please keep taking minutes.
choices.reaction: Agnes produces a second notebook, for the minutes about the minutes.

effects.memory: Agnes Thimble joined and became Keeper of the Minutes.

choices.label: We don’t really do minutes.
choices.reaction: “Noted,” says Agnes, and writes it down.

effects.memory: Agnes Thimble joined, uninvited, with a notebook.

speaker: gary
text: I painted a symbol on the garage door to make it look official. It’s a {thing}. People have started drawing it on things.

choices.label: Adopt it as our symbol.
choices.reaction: Within a month, the {thing} is on forty notebooks, a car and one forearm.

choices.label: Paint over it.
choices.reaction: Gary paints over it. The outline is still visible on sunny days. People say it is watching.

speaker: gary
text: I finished the book! It’s about whales. Did you know some whales sing songs that change every year? Can I talk about whales at the next {meeting}?

choices.label: Whales are relevant now.
choices.reaction: Gary’s whale talk runs fifty minutes. Afterwards, three people say it was the most moving thing they have heard in years.

choices.label: Gary.
choices.reaction: “Gary,” agrees Gary.

text: Evening. I’ve counted thirty-one people going into that garage this week. Either you’re running a business, a band or a cult. Which is it?

choices.label: “A book club.”
choices.reaction: Mr. Hedges narrows his eyes. He has read books. This is not that.

choices.label: “Come in and see.”
choices.reaction: Mr. Hedges stays until midnight. He brings his own folding chair the following week.

text: I joined a book club to check. They’ve never heard of you. Also, why does everyone leave your garage talking about {belief}?

choices.label: “It’s an advanced book club.”
choices.reaction: By Friday, the street believes the garage is an advanced book club, which is somehow worse.

choices.label: “Fine. Join us.”
choices.reaction: Mr. Hedges joins. Within a month he is the most devoted member on the street.

speaker: priya
text: We collected fourteen dollars in the soup jar, two buttons and a bus token. Martin wants a budget meeting. Dez wants a megaphone.

choices.label: Buy the megaphone.
choices.reaction: Dez’s first announcement through the megaphone is “testing.” His second is “TESTING.”

choices.label: Start a real fund.
choices.reaction: Martin opens a spreadsheet titled FUND. It has one row.

text: My husband thinks this is a cult. I told him it’s just {belief}. He asked what that means. I realized I don’t know.

choices.label: Bring him to a {meeting}.
choices.reaction: He comes, eats three bowls of something and leaves with a pamphlet he did not ask for.

choices.label: Tell him it’s a book club.
choices.reaction: It is the fourth time this month someone has used the book club excuse. Gary feels seen.

speaker: any
text: Members keep asking what we actually believe. The most common answer is “{practice1}.” The second most common is “I thought this was a book club.” Should we write something down?

choices.label: Write it down. Make it official.
choices.reaction: The founding statement is one page long. Agnes, or someone like her, has already found a typo. The typo is now doctrine.

choices.label: We believe whatever feels right.
choices.reaction: Everyone nods. Everyone nods at something different.

speaker: champion:practice
text: Something is catching on. After every {meeting}, a few members have started {practice}. Nobody organized it. It just happened. People seem to love it.

choices.label: Encourage it.
choices.reaction: Within a week, {practice} is simply what {members} do.

choices.label: Gently discourage it.
choices.reaction: It continues in the parking lot, where it is technically not our responsibility.

speaker: any
text: The {practice1Noun} people and the {practice2Noun} people both want the last half hour of every {meeting}. There have been words. One of the words was “heresy.”

choices.label: Put {practice1} first.
choices.hint: One custom rises · The other side sulks
choices.reaction: The losing side announces an “informal extension” in the parking lot.

choices.label: Put {practice2} first.
choices.reaction: The losing side announces an “informal extension” in the parking lot.

speaker: martin
text: I’ve written some house rules! Rule one: everyone gets a chair. Rule two: Gary gets the good chair. There are fourteen more, and they’re mostly about snacks.

choices.label: Adopt Martin’s rules.
choices.reaction: Martin reads all sixteen rules aloud. Nobody shouts, though several people want to.

choices.label: We don’t need rules yet.
choices.reaction: Martin folds the rules very small and puts them in his wallet, for later.

speaker: dez
text: I made posters. They say “{Movement}: IT’S HAPPENING.” I put up four hundred of them. Some are on the police station.

choices.label: Leave them up.
choices.reaction: People are asking what is happening. This is, Dez points out, the point.

choices.label: Take down the police station ones.
choices.reaction: Dez takes them down and puts them up again on the library, which he considers neutral ground.

text: Afternoon. Someone has covered the station noticeboard in posters saying something is happening. Is something happening? We’d like to know in advance.

choices.label: Invite the police officer to a {meeting}.
choices.reaction: Officer Haversham attends in uniform, stays out of uniform, and leaves humming.

choices.label: “Nothing is happening.”
choices.reaction: The police officer writes “NOTHING HAPPENING” in a notebook and underlines it.

speaker: gary
text: Quick thing. I’ve been introducing myself as Vice President. Nobody stopped me, so I assumed it was fine. Is it fine?

choices.label: Congratulations, Vice President Gary.
choices.reaction: Gary is given a lanyard. He wears it to the supermarket.

effects.memory: Gary became Vice President, by introducing himself as Vice President.

choices.label: We don’t have vice presidents.
choices.reaction: Gary nods and starts introducing himself as Deputy Vice President.

speaker: priya
text: It’s freezing in the garage. Half the members wear coats indoors. I could make the soup hotter, we could buy a heater, or we could make the cold part of it.

choices.label: Buy a heater.
choices.reaction: The heater smells faintly of burnt dust. People love it immediately.

choices.label: The cold builds character.
choices.reaction: Within a month, members describe being slightly cold as “the {movement} way.”

speaker: dez
text: Honestly? I feel like nobody listens to my ideas. I have SO many ideas. I have a notebook. It’s mostly ideas.

choices.label: Pick your best idea. We’ll do it.
choices.reaction: Dez’s best idea is a parade. It is approved, and then it is a parade.

choices.label: Maybe fewer ideas.
choices.reaction: Dez writes “fewer ideas” in the notebook. It is, technically, another idea.

speaker: martin
text: We’ve outgrown the garage. Gary’s car hasn’t been inside since spring. The community hall is available on {day}s for forty dollars.

choices.label: Rent the hall.
choices.reaction: Gary helps carry the chairs. He keeps one, for old times’ sake.

effects.memory: {Movement} moved out of Gary’s garage and into the community hall.

choices.label: We stay in the garage. It’s where it began.
choices.reaction: People start lining up down the driveway. Gary sets out snacks for the line.

effects.memory: {Movement} refused to leave Gary’s garage. People lined up down the driveway.
